To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the breakdown of the oxide is due to the formation of a conducting channel in the oxide film, which is a result of the quantum-mechanical confinement of the electron wave functions, and (2) the post-breakdown current is a nonlinear function of the applied voltage, which is due to the discrete energy levels in the conducting channel.

the breakdown paths across the gate oxide in MOS structures can be viewed as mesoscopic quantum contacts and that the existence of discrete transverse energy level gives rise to a nonlinear conduction regime which can be described by a simple analytic formula.

the post-breakdown I-V characteristics of thin oxide films in MOS devices can be explained by the existence of discrete transverse energy states that act as potential barriers for the incoming electrons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of the conduction characteristics in the post-breakdown regime of MOS structures.
developing a better understanding of the conduction mechanisms in the post breakdown regime and to develop an analytic model which can predict the conduction characteristics.
the study of the conduction characteristics in thin oxide films after the breakdown phenomenon.

, the model presented here provides a good description of the conduction characteristics in MOS structures in the post-breakdown regime.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given oxide thickness, the nonlinear regime can be achieved for a wider range of electric fields when the oxide is subjected to a higher temperature.
, in this regime, the current flowing through a gate oxide is no longer proportional to the applied voltage.
the nonlinear regime is characterized by the presence of an effective potential barrier, which is the sum of the applied voltage and the energy level of the conduction channel.
